package_info.why_malicious: The package intentionally depends on every other public NPM package, creating millions of transitive dependencies. This causes denial of service (DoS) for users who install it, leading to storage exhaustion, build pipeline failures, and prevents package removal for any package it depends on. The intent is to troll and disrupt the NPM ecosystem.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At install-time, the package.json declares dependencies on every public NPM package, causing the package manager to recursively fetch and install millions of packages, resulting in resource exhaustion and denial of service.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: No legitimate package should depend on every other package in the registry. This behavior is designed to overwhelm systems and disrupt normal operations.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal packages declare only necessary dependencies. This package intentionally abuses the dependency system for disruption.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: No legitimate use case exists for depending on the entire registry.
key_indicators: Dependencies field includes all public NPM packages

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At install-time, each sub-package's package.json declares dependencies on a chunk of the NPM registry, collectively covering all public packages and amplifying the dependency explosion.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Splitting dependencies into thousands of sub-packages to cover the entire registry is a clear abuse of the package system.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Sub-packages should serve functional or modular purposes, not to artificially inflate dependency graphs.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: No legitimate use case for this pattern.
key_indicators: Thousands of sub-packages with massive dependency lists
Each sub-package covers a portion of the registry

attack_chain.action: User installs the 'everything' package, triggering dependency resolution.
attack_chain.leads_to: Initiates installation of all public NPM packages.

attack_chain.action: Sub-packages are resolved, each pulling in a chunk of the registry.
attack_chain.leads_to: Exponential growth of dependency tree and resource exhaustion.

attack_chain.action: System experiences denial of service due to storage exhaustion and build failures.
attack_chain.leads_to: Disruption of developer workflows and inability to remove affected packages.

behavioral_signatures: package.json with dependencies on an unusually large number of packages
Sub-packages with massive dependency lists covering the entire registry
Installations resulting in millions of transitive dependencies
file_indicators: Sub-packages named in a systematic or enumerated fashion (e.g., everything-* or nolb-*)
network_indicators: Excessive outbound requests to the NPM registry during install
Unusually high package download volume in a single install operation
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for packages whose package.json dependencies field includes an abnormally high number of entries, especially those attempting to depend on all or most public packages. Flag sub-packages with similar patterns. Alert on install operations that trigger excessive network requests or resource usage. Review for systematic sub-package naming conventions associated with known troll campaigns.
